title: Meat Offered to Idols
lead: In the Greek and Roman world much of the meat on sale came from temple sacrifices, and temple dining rooms hosted weddings and club dinners. Whether a follower of Jesus could eat it was a live question from the Jerusalem Council (Acts 15:29) to Corinth (1 Corinthians 8-10) to the letters to Pergamum and Thyatira (Revelation 2:14, 20). Paul's answer in Corinth is not a flat yes or no: idols are nothing, yet a Christian does not eat in an idol's temple, and may be asked to give up a right for the sake of a weaker brother or sister.
